newsitem.title: KAZAKHSTAN: RAINFALL MAY HIT KAZAKH GRAIN QUALITY - OFFICIAL.
newsitem.headline: RAINFALL MAY HIT KAZAKH GRAIN QUALITY - OFFICIAL.

text.p: Rainfall could disrupt the Kazakh grain harvest, due to start next week in the former Soviet republic's northern grain belt, a senior grain institute official said on Friday.

"The northern harvest will start on August 15," Onal Shegebayev, director of the republic's Grain Farming Research Institute in Shortandy, 1,300 km northwest of the capital Almaty, told Reuters by telephone.
"It started raining two or three days ago," said Shegebayev. "This will not affect the harvest for the moment but if it continues after August 20, quality will be affected," he said.
Around 17 million hectares were sown to grains this year in Kazakhstan.
Last year's grain harvest, hit by drought, weighed in at 11.6 million tonnes, just over half the amount once gathered in Soviet times.
But Kazakhstan remains the largest grain exporter in the Commonwealth of Independent States, delivering 4-5 million tonnes abroad each year, much of it going to Russia.
Shegebayev said his forecast for this year's grain harvest stood at 13-14 million tonnes clean weight.
"Fuel for the harvest remains a big problem," he said. "Although farmers have begun to receive fuel and the government has promised there will be enough".
Earlier this year, the government ordered state and private oil companies to provide cash-strapped farms with fuel in exchange for grain futures contracts.
Shegebayev said harvesting in Kazakhstan's less important southern regions was complete but he had no details on how much grain was brought in.
